_comment: OTA trust anchors for update.json and the OTA package.
WHAT THIS FILE IS
The pinned public keys that xrom_ota_installer and the recovery gate verify
against. Installed to /system_ext/etc/xrom/ota-trust/ota_trust_anchors.json on
an AVB-verified, dm-verity-covered, read-only partition and labelled
xrom_ota_trust_file. There is no code path anywhere in this tree that adds an
anchor from a fetched file, from a partition an OTA writes, or from a system
property. A trust anchor that can be loaded at runtime is not a trust anchor.
WHY A SEPARATE FILE FROM security/payload_trust/trust_anchors.json
Different keys, different rotation schedule, different consumers. sepolicy
denies xrom_ota_installer access to the payload anchors, so compromising the
OTA path cannot reach the keys that decide what may run inside a pVM.
WHY TWO ENTRIES PER RELEASE
require_dual_signature is on by default, so a manifest and its package need
BOTH an Ed25519 and an RSA-4096 signature under two DISTINCT key ids. The AND
does not defend against Ed25519 being broken; it defends against a bug in one
verification path and against the compromise of one signing key, which are the
two failures that actually happen. The cost is real and should not be hidden:
two keys, two ceremonies, two rotation schedules, and a signing tool that fails
if either one is missing. See correction #8 in docs/05.
THESE ARE DEVELOPMENT KEYS
Both entries are enabled because a build with no enabled anchor cannot install
anything, which is the correct state for a release build with no real keys but
not a usable state for bring-up. The private halves were generated outside this
repository and are NOT committed; only the public halves are. Before a release
image is built both entries must be replaced with production keys, and
tools/xrom_preflight.py fails the build if a development anchor is still enabled.

anchors.purpose: OTA manifest and package signature (second of the dual pair)
anchors._note: DEVELOPMENT KEY, 4096-bit modulus. Replace before release.
